title: How does 23 × 27 change when 23 grows by 2 and 27 grows by 5?
description: A dot diagram of twenty three rows and twenty seven columns gains two rows and five columns, and splits into four blocks. Adding every block gives twenty five times thirty two. Keeko doubts that the corner block can be left out.
teaching_notes: One idea: two numbers that grow split the diagram into four parts, and all four must be added. Watch for students who add the two strips and forget the corner.

source: 23 × 27 = 621. Use the four parts to find the product when 23 grows by 2 and 27 grows by 5.
video_script.why: The child has met growth by one. Here both numbers grow by any amount, and the diagram splits into four parts.
video_script.substitution: Name the four parts of the grown diagram, work out each one from the numbers, and add them all to the old total.
video_script.anchor: the dot diagram of twenty three rows and twenty seven columns, with new rows below and new columns on the right
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko adds only the two new strips to six hundred twenty one and leaves out the corner. The corner holds two rows of five dots, so ten dots go missing and the total comes out at seven hundred ninety.
video_script.payoff_line: Every one of the four parts must be added

final_answer.spoken: twenty five times thirty two is eight hundred, an increase of one hundred seventy nine

never_show: a total that leaves out the corner, marked as right
maths_rules: (a + m)(b + n) = ab + mb + an + mn
leaving out the corner gives 621 + 54 + 115 = 790, which is 10 too few
video_script.design: One idea: two growing numbers give four parts, and all four are added. Assumes the dot diagram and the distributive property. Wrong idea: the corner can be left out. The diagram with its four blocks stays through the idea and the doubt.

narration: <bookmark mark='block'/>Take eigh rows of dots, with b dots in each row. That block is eigh times b.
<bookmark mark='more'/>Add m more rows below, and n more columns on the right.
<bookmark mark='four'/>Together the diagram has four blocks.
The new rows alone are m times b. The new columns alone are eigh times n.
The corner is m times n.

narration: <bookmark mark='vals'/>Step one, match the numbers to the letters. Eigh is twenty three and m is two.
The number b is twenty seven, and n is five.
<bookmark mark='rule'/>The four parts rule gives the new total.
It is eigh b, plus m b, plus eigh n, plus m n.

beats.colours: each part in its own colour
narration: <bookmark mark='mb'/>Step two, work out each new part. The part m b is two times twenty seven, which is fifty four.
<bookmark mark='an'/>The part eigh n is twenty three times five, which is one hundred fifteen.
<bookmark mark='mn'/>The part m n is two times five, which is ten.

marks.sum: = 800 is written, and the new product 25 × 32 beside it

narration: <bookmark mark='add'/>Step three, add all four parts to the old total.
That is six hundred twenty one, plus fifty four, plus one hundred fifteen, plus ten.
<bookmark mark='sum'/>The sum is eight hundred, which is twenty five times thirty two.
<bookmark mark='inc'/>Step four, the increase is the three new parts together.
Fifty four, plus one hundred fifteen, plus ten, is one hundred seventy nine.
<bookmark mark='check'/>Check it. Eight hundred take away six hundred twenty one is one hundred seventy nine.

marks.pay: the words every one of the four parts must be added appear

narration: <bookmark mark='pay'/>Every one of the four parts must be added.
<bookmark mark='ans'/>Twenty five times thirty two is eight hundred, an increase of one hundred seventy nine.

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks we can leave out the corner and add only the two new strips.
<bookmark mark='corner'/>But the corner is made of real dots. It has two rows of five dots.
<bookmark mark='strike'/>Without it, the total is seven hundred ninety, which is ten too few.
